title: Open/closed localization for ordinary derived condensed module objects
statement: For a commutative condensed ring Λ, a closed immersion i:Z→X and complementary quasi-compact open immersion j:U→X, on ordinary unbounded derived supportModules: the open extension/restriction unit and the closed inverse/direct image counit are invertible; the closed unit is invertible on objects with zero open restriction; the mixed restrictions i* j! and j* i_* vanish; and the two restrictions jointly detect isomorphisms. The units and counits are the actual adjunction maps of [def-sfb-open-closed-internal-hom-comparisons]. No boundedness or constructibility hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tags 09AA, 09AH, 09BN; lift of the abelian support calculation to module objects, followed by exact derived functors.

proof.text: The faithful conservative forgetful functor from module objects detects zero objects and isomorphisms. Lift the abelian supported-unit and closed-counit maps using mapModAdjunction. The support coefficient equivalence transports them by invertible units and counits. Lift the abelian open-extension unit via mapModLeftAdjunction, then transport scalars along alpha.

The underlying open restriction of a closed image is zero, since it evaluates sections on empty base changes. If both module restrictions vanish, the supported closed unit identifies the module with the direct image of zero. Exactness then detects isomorphisms by the kernels and cokernels.

Apply the canonical exact derived-functor composition and natural-isomorphism APIs to the invertible ordinary open unit and closed counit. Their derived functors are fully faithful, so the actual derived unit and counit are invertible. Exact functors commute with homology, hence ordinary joint detection passes to derived morphisms, and the mixed closed image vanishes on every homology object.

Restrict the supported derived closed unit: the closed restriction is invertible by its triangle identity and invertible counit; the open restriction is a map between zero objects. Joint detection proves the unit invertible. Finally, transpose the identity of i* j! L through i* adjoint to i_* and j! adjoint to j*: it lands in a Hom group into j* i_*=0. Thus i* j! L has zero identity. Empty strata and zero coefficients satisfy the same argument.

lean.statement:
theorem condensedSupportDerivedLocalization {Z U X : Scheme.{u}}
    (i : Z ⟶ X) (j : U ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i] [IsOpenImmersion j] [QuasiCompact j]
    (hij : Set.range i.base = (Set.range j.base)ᶜ) :
    (∀ L, IsIso ((openSupportDerivedAdjunction Λ j).unit.app L)) ∧
    (∀ P, IsIso ((closedPullbackDerivedAdjunction Λ i).counit.app P)) ∧
    (∀ M : DerivedCategory (supportModules Λ X),
      IsZero ((supportPullback Λ j).mapDerivedCategory.obj M) →
        IsIso ((closedPullbackDerivedAdjunction Λ i).unit.app M)) ∧
    (∀ L, IsZero ((supportPullback Λ i).mapDerivedCategory.obj
      ((openImmersionLowerShriek Λ j).mapDerivedCategory.obj L))) ∧
    (∀ P, IsZero ((supportPullback Λ j).mapDerivedCategory.obj
      ((lowerStar Λ i).mapDerivedCategory.obj P))) ∧
    (∀ {M N : DerivedCategory (supportModules Λ X)} (f : M ⟶ N),
      IsIso ((supportPullback Λ i).mapDerivedCategory.map f) →
      IsIso ((supportPullback Λ j).mapDerivedCategory.map f) → IsIso f)
